**File:** `core/src/map/builder.ts`

**Module note rule** (lines 291–306, hash at line 351): bottom-up, deepest first. A module is rewritten when it is *covered* — every file in it has a fresh note and every child module already has a note — **and** its deterministic hash differs from the stored one. The hash is `sha1` over all `path:noteHash` pairs for its files and its children, so it changes the moment any file below it got a new note or any child module was rewritten.

**Project note rule** (lines 318–330): only when the root module (`''`) has a note **and** the project hash — `sha1` over all `path:moduleHash` pairs — differs from the stored project hash. Since the root module's hash depends on all child module hashes, the project note is effectively rewritten whenever any module note was rewritten in the same build.

Now I have the full picture. Here's what happens:

---

**When the model's answer doesn't parse as the expected form**

The chain is: `forcedJson` → `askAgain` → the per-note method → `build()`.

1. **`forcedJson` swallows everything into `null`.** It calls `JSON.parse(text)` and catches any error — malformed JSON, empty content, server refusal — and returns `null` (core/src/session/forced-json.ts:82–86). The caller never sees the raw error.

2. **`askAgain` retries once.** The `ask` method (builder.ts:200) calls `forcedJson`. `askAgain` (builder.ts:210) checks the result: if it's `null` and the signal hasn't aborted, it appends the string `BRIEFER` — *"Answer more briefly: one sentence per field, fewer items."* — to the last user message and calls `ask` a second time with **1.5× the token budget** (builder.ts:215–217). If the retry also returns `null`, `askAgain` returns `null` and the note method returns `null`.

3. **The per-note method (`fileNote`, `moduleNote`, `projectNote`) propagates the `null`.** Each calls `askAgain`, then runs its own `parse*` function (`parseFileNote`, `parseModuleNote`, `parseProjectNote`). If the raw result is `null` or the parser rejects it, the method returns `null` — no note is written, no file is saved.

---

**How the person finds out which notes failed**

There are three places the failure surface:

1. **The progress message in the Map tab.** At the end of `build()`, the result's `failed` array is formatted into the progress message (builder.ts:334–335):
   ```
   N file notes, N module notes, the project note; 2 failed (core/src/map/builder.ts, core/src/map/notes.ts)
   ```
   The first three paths are shown; anything beyond that is truncated with `…, …`.

2. **The toast on completion.** When `map.progress` fires with phase `done`, `stopped`, or `failed`, the Map tab pushes a toast with that message (map-tab.tsx:98–99). A `failed` phase (which is a *hard* exception, not a parse failure) pushes an error toast with the exception message instead.

3. **The tree labels.** Files and modules that never received a note keep the dim label **no note** in the tree (map-tab.tsx:144, 163), so the person can see exactly which items were skipped and click them to see the "missing" note.

The `result.failed` array itself is part of `MapBuildResult` (builder.ts:75) and contains the raw paths — `core/src/map/builder.ts` for files, `core/src/map/` for modules, and `Project` for the project note — but the UI never exposes the array directly; it only renders the truncated message string.

Here's the full lifecycle, with the three files that matter:

---

### 1. When it is made — `core/src/session/session.ts` (line ~2706)

The contract is distilled **once, up front, before the model says a word** on a task-shaped request. In `send()`:

```ts
if (this.gateProfile !== 'off' && (sendOpts?.distill ?? looksLikeTask(text)) && looksLikeTask(text)) {
  const contract = await distillContract(
    this.opts.client, this.transcript.messages(), userText, signal, this.stepSchemas(),
    { lean: this.gateProfile === 'fast' },
  )
  …
  this.meta.contract = contract
  this.opts.store?.saveMeta(this.meta)
}
```

`looksLikeTask` (also in `contract.ts:101`) gates on length ≥ 220 chars, or ≥ 80 chars with ≥ 3 sentences — deliberately dumb, tuned so the ~8–15 s generation cost is only paid when the task will run for minutes. The caller can override via `sendOpts.distill` (the host knows the raw typed text; the unattended runner marks its own nudges). A failed distillation costs nothing — the turn runs without a contract, exactly as before contracts existed.

Each new task-shaped message **re-distills and replaces** the whole contract, so a second big request is not gated against the first one's criteria. Short follow-ups ("and fix the indent too") are not task-shaped, so the running task's contract survives them.

---

### 2. Where it goes in the transcript — `core/src/session/session.ts` (line ~2732)

After distillation, the rendered contract is **folded into the user message itself**, not appended as a separate message:

```ts
turnText = `[${renderContract(contract)}]\n\n${promptText}`
```

This keeps the contract inside the same bracketed user message the window strips one level from on replay. The contract object is also persisted to `this.meta.contract` via `this.opts.store?.saveMeta(this.meta)`, so it survives a resumed session.

---

### 3. How it survives compaction — `core/src/session/session.ts` (line ~3831) and `core/src/agent/prompt.ts` (line ~319)

Compaction does **not** copy the contract into the summary text. Instead, it **rebuilts message 0 (the system prompt) from scratch** and passes the rendered contract into it:

```ts
// session.ts:3814 — inside applyCompactionSwap
content: buildSystemPrompt({
  …
  ...(this.meta.contract !== undefined && this.meta.contract.satisfied !== true
    ? { contract: renderContract(this.meta.contract) } : {}),
  …
})
```

`buildSystemPrompt` in `core/src/agent/prompt.ts:319` appends it to the prompt body:

```ts
if (opts.contract !== undefined && opts.contract !== '') parts.push('', opts.contract)
```

The contract is placed **before memory and notes** — with the other task-specific listings — because information in the prefix is the lever that measurably routes this model. A satisfied contract (`contract.satisfied === true`) is history and stays out; only a live, unsatisfied contract is promoted.

Because message 0 is rebuilt (not edited) at every swap, the contract survives every compaction automatically — no new mechanism, no risk of forgetting it. The `checkedState` field (set by the acceptance gate after each writing turn) is part of what `renderContract` emits, so the model sees not just what "done" means but where criteria actually stand after each swap.

---

**The file that decides is `core/src/session/slot-record.ts`.**

Here's the mechanism:

### One file per workspace, not per session

llama.cpp's KV-cache state is huge — roughly 23 MiB per 1,000 tokens, so a 20k-token session is ~453 MiB. Storing one per session would quickly fill gigabytes. Instead, the workspace has exactly **one** `.bin` file, overwritten on each save. The filename is deterministic:

```
privatecode-<12-hex-chars>.bin
```

where the 12 hex chars are the first 12 characters of `SHA-1(lowercased(workspaceRoot))`. Because it's derived from the workspace root, the same workspace always maps to the same file name — but different workspaces get different names. The server only receives the plain basename (no path), so PrivateCode owns both the label and the location.

### How a session resumes

Each save is accompanied by a small JSON label file (`slot.json`) in the workspace's private state directory, recording three fields:

```ts
{ sessionId, savedAt, tokens }
```

When the app starts a session, `host.ts` (line 1264) calls `session.restoreSlot()`, which:

1. Reads `slot.json` via `readSlotRecord()`.
2. **Rejects** the file if the record is missing or if `record.sessionId !== this.id` — i.e. only the session that last saved gets to resume. A stale `.bin` belonging to another session is harmless; it's simply ignored.
3. If it matches, calls `client.slotRestore(filename)`, which loads the KV state in ~0.5 s (vs. minutes of re-prefill).
4. Sets `promptCacheCold = false` and `slotJustRestored = true`, so the subsequent `warmPrefix()` only prefill the tail of the transcript gained since the save.

### When the file is written

`saveSlotIfDue()` (line 4309) writes the slot only after a turn completes with the model's final message — never mid-turn, because the slot holds a prefix of the transcript and a saved sequence that the next prompt diverges from is worthless. It throttles writes to every **3 minutes** (`SLOT_SAVE_INTERVAL_MS`) **or** when the transcript has grown by **20,000 tokens** (`SLOT_SAVE_GROWTH_TOKENS`), whichever comes first. A crash loses only the prefill of turns since the last save, not the whole session.

### Why exactly one file

The comment on line 16–18 of `slot-record.ts` explains it directly:

> "one file per workspace, overwritten: the session you were last in resumes instantly, older ones prefill in the background as they always did, and the disk holds one state per workspace instead of one per session that ever existed (a 100k-token state is ~2.3 GB)."

The record file (`slot.json`) is the label that answers "which session does this one file belong to?" — and it's the only thing that gates restoration.
